blockers.question: Which artefact should the FNB submission be — an APK or an AAB? (The app identity, android.package / ios.bundleIdentifier, is the separate half of this blocker and is still open.)
blockers.why_blocked: It decides the entire build path: an APK is installed directly by judges and needs no store account or review; an AAB requires a Google Play listing, a developer account, and review time. No eas.json or package identifier exists, so no build can start either way.
options: AAB, via a Google Play store listing
blockers.recommendation: APK. Judges install an app; they do not browse a store listing, so an APK removes review time and developer-account setup from the critical path.
blockers.answer: APK. Not an AAB, not a store submission.

blockers.question: Confirm the permanent app identifier 'za.co.varsitycompanion' for android.package and ios.bundleIdentifier, and confirm an Expo account email to use for EAS.
blockers.why_blocked: The identifier is permanent once an app is published and cannot be changed later. EAS builds also require an Expo account — the build runs in Expo's cloud, not on this machine. Neither exists yet.
options: A different name tied to the business entity
blockers.recommendation: za.co.varsitycompanion. It matches the .co.za domain and the product name, and it is the kind of identifier a South African business keeps.
blockers.note_2026_10_21: CORRECTION: email is NOT a requirement. An Expo account needs an email only to register - using an existing free address (Gmail etc.) costs nothing. The email was never the blocker; the real blocker is (a) no Expo account/login exists, and (b) no free iOS path. Also found: no Java, Android SDK or Gradle on this machine, so a LOCAL apk build would need a large install before EAS can be avoided.
blockers.revised_question: Confirm the app identifier za.co.varsitycompanion, and decide: FNB likely requires the iOS app too (the original ask). iOS builds cannot be produced without an Apple Developer account (~R1300/yr) or a Mac. If Android-only APK is acceptable for the FNB submission, that can be built with a free Expo account.

blockers.question: The production materials library only contains data for COS132 (15 rows). Every other module returns 0 results. To populate it I need the production DATABASE_URL (the Neon Postgres connection string) from the Render dashboard, or the founder runs the ingest script with it.
blockers.why_blocked: scripts/ingest_real_materials.py connects through the app's SessionLocal, which reads DATABASE_URL. The local .env points at the local Docker database (127.0.0.1:5544/varsity_companion_dev), not production. The production value lives only in Render's environment variables and has never been copied here. I will not ask for it in chat - it is a credential.
blockers.context: This is user 11's complaint ('the manual labour of having to add files and all, that is a lot'). It is NOT a code defect: search works, the ingest script is dynamic and already handles any module code. Measured against production with a real session: COS132 -> 15 materials; COS101, COS110, CSC301, MAM201, EKN110, FNB152, WTW165 -> 0 each. A judge who types their own module code gets an empty screen and concludes they must paste everything by hand.
options: Founder runs, on a machine with the production DATABASE_URL set: venv/bin/python scripts/ingest_real_materials.py  (idempotent; upserts)
Founder copies DATABASE_URL from Render into the local .env, then I run it
Leave it and pre-ingest only after the hackathon dashboard work is done
blockers.recommendation: Option 1 or 2 before Friday. It is the single highest-impact fix for the demo: it turns 'Find Materials' from empty into useful for any module a judge types.
blockers.answer: PARTLY UNBLOCKED, tested live. The per-module ingest endpoint works: POST /materials/modules/CSC301/ingest returned inserted=8 in 62s, and CSC301 then returned 5 searchable materials (PDFs + articles). The student-facing 'Find resources for this module' button calls exactly this. So user 11 does NOT need the production DB credential: a student can populate any module themselves. What remains blocked is only the OPTIONAL bulk pre-seed via scripts/ingest_real_materials.py for common module codes.
blockers.remaining: Optional: bulk pre-seed common SA module codes before the demo so a judge's first search is never empty. Requires the production DATABASE_URL (founder).
